Simplified all 8 Python node modules: removed PROJECT_PATH_REMINDER/WP_SCOPE_REMINDER imports and f-string extra construction from developer/qa/reviewer/docs/security_auditor/release_engineer; removed preamble and project_path_reminder from pm and added plan_file; removed project_path_reminder from synthesis.

comments.note: PROJECT_PATH_REMINDER and WP_SCOPE_REMINDER constants in __init__.py are now unused by any node module but must remain because test_public_constants_importable_from_nodes asserts their importability from src.nodes. A future cleanup WP could remove the constants and update that test simultaneously.

The pm.md template now uses {{> pm-preamble}} unconditionally (no {{#if}} guard), which is a slight structural divergence from the old {{#if preamble}}…{{/if}} pattern. This is intentional — PM always receives a plan_file and the preamble is always needed.

summary: All 7 acceptance criteria verified against template source files and test suite output.
AC1: grep confirms zero occurrences of {project_path_reminder} / {wp_scope_reminder} in any rendered template (VARIABLES.md references are documentation-only).
AC2–AC6: All 8 templates manually inspected — partial include directives match spec exactly, including conditional guards.

comments.note: No issues found — all templates and node modules are clean and consistent with the WP spec.

synthesis.py intentionally omits wp_id from its render_prompt call (synthesis operates at project level, no current WP). This is correct behaviour and the template's lack of a {{#if wp_id}} block is consistent with that design.
pm.md pm-preamble is unconditional (no {{#if}} guard) — consistent with the developer's note that PM always receives a plan_file. No issue.

summary: PASS with Fix-Forward applied. All 8 stage node modules and templates are clean, consistent, and correctly implement the WP-003 partial-include pattern.

Fix-Forward applied: VARIABLES.md contained stale duplicate code examples (the pre-WP-003 PM and Synthesis usage patterns) that should have been removed. The Notes section also referenced the obsolete WP_SCOPE_REMINDER.format() guidance and old variable-based layer descriptions. Removed the duplicate sections and updated the Notes to describe the current partial-based approach.

Node module architecture is excellent: module-level _TEMPLATE caching avoids repeated disk reads, prompt builders are uniformly minimal (project_path + wp_id only), and the pattern is perfectly consistent across all 7 WP-scoped stages.

Template structure verified against all 7 AC criteria: partial includes correct, conditional {{#if wp_id}} guards in correct positions, pm.md unconditional pm-preamble is intentional and well-documented.

Orphaned PROJECT_PATH_REMINDER / WP_SCOPE_REMINDER constants in __init__.py are correctly left in place (test_public_constants_importable_from_nodes requires them). Developer already flagged this for future cleanup.

comments.note: VARIABLES.md contained stale duplicate code sections: a second '### PM stage' block and a second '### Synthesis stage' block showing the pre-WP-003 API (PROJECT_PATH_REMINDER, preamble variables). These are misleading dead examples that would confuse anyone adding a new node type. Removed both stale blocks. The active, correct examples above them remain intact.

VARIABLES.md Notes section: removed the stale first bullet ('WP_SCOPE_REMINDER is a format string...') which no longer applies since constants are not passed as template variables. Updated the two-layer scope reinforcement bullet to reference the current partial names ({{> wp-scope-reminder}}, {{> scope-restriction}}) instead of the old variable names (wp_scope_reminder, extra SCOPE RESTRICTION block).

Module-level _TEMPLATE = load_template('stage') caching is a well-chosen pattern — templates are loaded once at import time and reused across all invocations of the node. This avoids repeated disk I/O per agent run.

The orphaned PROJECT_PATH_REMINDER and WP_SCOPE_REMINDER constants in __init__.py are correctly preserved for test compatibility. Developer's note about a future cleanup WP is appropriate — these are now zero-dependency-from-production constants kept solely for the test contract.

[documentation-forward] orchestrator/docs/architecture.md section on 'Two-layer prompt scope reinforcement' should be verified to reference the current partial-based implementation ({{> wp-scope-reminder}}, {{> scope-restriction}}) rather than the old Python variable approach, now that VARIABLES.md has been updated to match.
